# The lock file — fobos.lock

## What it records

After every successful `fobis fetch`, FoBiS writes `fobos.lock` **in the dependency directory**
(`.fobis_deps/fobos.lock` by default, `<deps_dir>/fobos.lock` when `[dependencies] deps_dir` is set). It records,
for every fetched dependency, the exact commit its specification resolved to and a SHA-256 checksum of its files:

```ini
# fobos.lock — auto-generated by FoBiS.py fetch — do not edit by hand

[PENF]
url    = https://github.com/szaghi/PENF
commit = a1b2c3d4e5f6789012345678901234567890abcd
sha256 = deadbeefdeadbeef...
tag    = v1.5.0

[stdlib]
url      = https://github.com/fortran-lang/stdlib
commit   = 9f8e7d6c5b4a3210fedcba9876543210fedcba98
sha256   = 0102030405060708...
semver   = ^0.5
resolved = v0.5.3
```

## It stays with the dependencies

The lock belongs to the fetched dependencies, not to the project's sources: the dependency directory is not
committed (add `.fobis_deps/` to `.gitignore`), and the lock with it. It is the record of what **this** checkout
fetched, so that FoBiS can tell when a dependency's clone moved away from it, and put it back.

What makes **every** checkout (a collaborator's, CI's, a release build's) fetch the same code is the specification
in the fobos: pin each dependency with `tag=` or `rev=`. A `branch=` or a bare URL follows the branch, and a `semver=`
constraint resolves to the newest matching tag when a checkout fetches for the first time.

## Lock verification

On every later `fobis fetch`, FoBiS compares each dependency's `HEAD` with the lock. A mismatch emits a warning
(non-fatal):

```
Warning: dependency 'PENF' HEAD (a1b2c3d) does not match
fobos.lock (deadbeef). Run 'fobis fetch --update' to refresh.
```

This typically means the dependency was changed outside FoBiS (a manual `git pull` inside its directory).

## Back to the lock (`--frozen`)

`fobis fetch --frozen` refuses to run without a lock, checks every dependency out at the commit the lock records,
uses the locked tag of a `semver=` constraint without asking the remote, and leaves the lock unchanged:

```bash
fobis fetch --frozen   # abort if .fobis_deps/fobos.lock is missing
```

It is meant for a checkout that keeps its fetched dependencies (a workstation, a cluster account, a CI job that
caches `.fobis_deps/`). On a fresh checkout there is no lock: run `fobis fetch`, and rely on the fobos's pins.

## Moving forward

```bash
fobis fetch --update   # move each dependency to the newest commit its specification allows, rewrite the lock
```

To move a pinned dependency, change its `tag=` or `rev=` in the fobos (that is the change to commit) and run
`fobis fetch --update`.

## Semver version constraints

Instead of pinning to an exact `tag=`, you can declare a version constraint:

```ini
[dependencies]
PENF   = https://github.com/szaghi/PENF :: semver=^1.5
stdlib = https://github.com/fortran-lang/stdlib :: semver=>=0.5,<1.0
```

`fobis fetch` queries the remote tags and resolves the highest tag satisfying
the constraint:

| Constraint | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `^1.5` | `>=1.5.0, <2.0.0` (compatible release) |
| `^1.5.2` | `>=1.5.2, <2.0.0` |
| `~1.5.2` | `>=1.5.2, <1.6.0` (patch-level) |
| `>=1.0,<2.0` | explicit range |
| `=1.5.0` | exact version |
| `*` | any version |

The resolved tag is written to the lock under `resolved`. On later
non-`--update` runs in the same checkout the locked tag is used without
re-querying the remote; a fresh checkout resolves the constraint again.

`semver=` cannot be combined with `tag=`, `branch=`, or `rev=` — they are
mutually exclusive.
